content:
Integers are Class 6's big new idea — numbers below zero. Ordering, absolute value and signed addition catch students who rush. Here is what the IMO Class 6 integers chapter tests, the sign rules, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 6 Maths Olympiad Integers chapter tests

  • Integers on the number line and ordering
  • Absolute value and opposites
  • Adding and subtracting integers (sign rules)
  • Real-life problems: temperature, sea level, profit-loss

Key facts your child should know

  • Every positive integer beats every negative — and −3 > −7.
  • |−7| = 7: absolute value is distance from zero.
  • Same signs: add and keep the sign. Different: subtract, take the bigger size's sign.
  • a − b = a + (−b) — subtracting is adding the opposite, so 3 − (−4) = 7.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Ordering −3 below −7 because 3 < 7.
  • Dropping the sign flip in 5 − (−2).
  • Treating a fall of 6° from −2°C as +4°C instead of −8°C.
